 The Medusa of classical myth was one of three female monsters, the Gorgons, daughters
of the sea-deities Phorcys and his sister Ceto. Dragon-like creatures who were crowned
with serpents, the three sisters inspired such terror that whoever looked upon them was
turned to stone. Alternatively, it was the power of their gaze that turned its objects to stone.
 Medusa, the only one of the three who was mortal, was slain by the hero Perseus (the son of
Zeus and Danae) who had been set the task of bringing her severed head to King Polydectes
in order that the king should agree to regulate his passion for Danae. In his struggle with
